title: Dependency injection
summary: @inject, service lifetimes, and what Scoped means per mode.

predict.title: A singleton counter
options: An error: a singleton can't be injected into a component
predict.explanation: On the server, a **Singleton is one object for the whole app**, so every user shares it. Bo sees Ana's clicks: **Clicks: 3**. Here it is only a counter, but with a cart or a user name it is a data leak. Per-user state should be **Scoped** (one per circuit).

predict.title: Scoped in Interactive Server
predict.body:
Program.cs (the whole app is Interactive Server, set in `App.razor`):

```csharp
builder.Services.AddScoped<CartService>();
```

`/products` has an **Add** button that calls `Cart.Add(product)`. `/cart` shows `@Cart.Items.Count`. Both pages use `@inject CartService Cart`.

In one tab, you click **Add** once on `/products`, then click a link to `/cart`. After that, you open `/cart` in a **new tab**.

**What do the two tabs show?**
predict.explanation: In Interactive Server, a Scoped service lives as long as the **circuit**. Navigating with a link inside the app keeps the same circuit, so the first tab still has the same `CartService`: **1**. A new tab opens a new circuit with a new instance: **0**. (To keep a cart across tabs, you need storage, like a database or browser storage.)

predict.title: The missing client registration
predict.body:
A Blazor Web App with Auto mode. `ITodoApi` is in the `.Client` project.

Server `Program.cs`:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddScoped<ITodoApi, ServerTodoApi>();
```

Client `Program.cs`:

```csharp
// nothing registered for ITodoApi
```

Todos.razor (in the `.Client` project):

```razor
@page "/todos"
@rendermode InteractiveAuto
@inject ITodoApi Api
```

The first visit works. A few visits later, when the WebAssembly files are downloaded and cached, you open `/todos` again.

**What happens?**
options: It still works: the browser calls the server's `ServerTodoApi`
The page shows, but the list is empty
An error: there is no registered service of type `ITodoApi`
A build error in the `.Client` project
predict.explanation: With Auto, the first visit runs on the **server**, where `ITodoApi` is registered. Once WebAssembly is ready, the component runs **in the browser** and asks the **client** container, which has no registration. It fails with *Cannot provide a value for property 'Api'... There is no registered service of type 'ITodoApi'*. Register an implementation (like one that calls an API with `HttpClient`) in the client `Program.cs` too. The build doesn't catch it: it is a runtime error.

predict.title: Two transients
options: An error: the same service is injected twice
It depends on the render mode
predict.explanation: **Transient** means a **new instance for every injection**, so `First` and `Second` are two objects with two different `Guid`s: **False**. With `AddScoped` or `AddSingleton`, both properties would get the same instance and it would show **True**.

practice.title: Register a service
practice.task:
You wrote `ICartService` and its class `CartService`. Each user must have their own cart.

In `Program.cs`, register `CartService` as the implementation of **`ICartService`**, with the right lifetime for per-user state, **before** `builder.Build()`.
practice.hint: Per-user state on the server is **Scoped**. The interface goes first: `AddScoped<ICartService, CartService>()`.

checks.label: `builder.Services.AddScoped<ICartService, CartService>()`
checks.hint: Add `builder.Services.AddScoped<ICartService, CartService>();`.

checks.label: Registered before `builder.Build()`
checks.hint: Services must be registered before `var app = builder.Build();`.

checks.label: Not a Singleton (that would share one cart with all users)
checks.hint: A Singleton on the server is shared by every user. Use `AddScoped`.

practice.title: Inject it in a page
practice.task:
Write the page **`/cart`**: 1. Inject **`ICartService`** into a property called **`Cart`**. 2. Inject **`NavigationManager`** into a property called **`Nav`**. 3. Show `

@Cart.Items.Count items

`. 4. A button that navigates to `/checkout`.
practice.hint: The syntax is `@inject Type PropertyName`, one per line, at the top of the file.

checks.label: `@inject ICartService Cart`
checks.hint: Add the line `@inject ICartService Cart`.

checks.label: `@inject NavigationManager Nav`
checks.hint: Add the line `@inject NavigationManager Nav`. It is built in, so there is nothing to register.

checks.label: Shows `@Cart.Items.Count`
checks.hint:
Write `

@Cart.Items.Count items

`.

checks.label: Calls `Nav.NavigateTo("/checkout")`
checks.hint: In the button: `@onclick="@(() => Nav.NavigateTo("/checkout"))"`.

practice.title: Inject in code-behind
practice.task:
The markup moved to `Cart.razor`, and the C# is in `Cart.razor.cs`. The two properties below are never set, so `Cart` is `null` at runtime.

Make the container fill **both** properties.
practice.hint: In C#, `@inject` becomes the **`[Inject]`** attribute on a property.

checks.label: `[Inject]` on `ICartService CartService`
checks.hint: Write `[Inject] public ICartService CartService { get; set; } = default!;`.

checks.label: `[Inject]` on `ILogger<Cart> Logger`
checks.hint: `ILogger<T>` is built in. Add `[Inject]` before it too.

checks.label: Still a `partial class Cart`
checks.hint: Keep `public partial class Cart`: it is the other half of `Cart.razor`.

checks.label: No `@inject` in a `.cs` file
checks.hint: `@inject` is Razor syntax. In C#, use `[Inject]`.

practice.title: Fix the data leak
practice.task:
This app is Interactive Server. Users report they sometimes see **another user's name** in the header.

- `UserSession` holds the current user's name and cart.
- `IWeatherCache` holds a public weather forecast that is the same for everyone (and is thread-safe).

Fix the registrations: per-user state must not be shared, and the shared cache should stay shared.
practice.hint: On the server, a Singleton is one object for **all users**. Which of the two holds per-user data?

checks.label: `UserSession` is Scoped
checks.hint: Use `builder.Services.AddScoped<UserSession>();`: one per circuit, so one per user and tab.

checks.label: `UserSession` is no longer a Singleton
checks.hint: Remove `AddSingleton<UserSession>()`.

checks.label: `IWeatherCache` stays a Singleton
checks.hint: Public, thread-safe data is fine as a Singleton. Keep `AddSingleton<IWeatherCache, WeatherCache>()`.

practice.title: Use a DbContext factory
practice.task:
This Interactive Server page injects `AppDbContext` directly. The context lives as long as the circuit, and quick clicks throw *A second operation was started on this context instance*.

`Program.cs` already calls `AddDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>(...)`. Change the page:

1. Inject **`IDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>`** as **`DbFactory`**.
2. In `OnInitializedAsync`, create a short-lived context with **`using var db = await DbFactory.CreateDbContextAsync();`** and load the products from it.
practice.hint: The factory gives you a new context each time. `using` disposes it at the end of the method.

checks.label: `@inject IDbContextFactory<AppDbContext> DbFactory`
checks.hint: Replace the first `@inject` with `@inject IDbContextFactory<AppDbContext> DbFactory`.

checks.label: No `@inject AppDbContext` any more
checks.hint: Don't inject the context itself in an interactive server component.

checks.label: `using var db = await DbFactory.CreateDbContextAsync();`
checks.hint: Inside `OnInitializedAsync`: `using var db = await DbFactory.CreateDbContextAsync();`.

checks.label: Loads products from the new context
checks.hint: Write `products = await db.Products.ToListAsync();` (lowercase `db`, the new context).

practice.title: Register for Auto, from scratch
practice.task:
A Blazor Web App uses **Auto** mode. `ITodoApi` lives in the `.Client` project, with two implementations:

- **`ServerTodoApi`** (server project) reads the database.
- **`HttpTodoApi`** (`.Client` project) calls the server's API with `HttpClient`.

In the textbox, under each comment, write the registrations for each `Program.cs`:

1. Server: `ITodoApi` → `ServerTodoApi`, **Scoped**.
2. Client: an `HttpClient` (Scoped) whose `BaseAddress` is `builder.HostEnvironment.BaseAddress`.
3. Client: `ITodoApi` → `HttpTodoApi`, **Scoped**.
practice.hint: Same interface, two containers, two implementations. The client's `HttpClient` registration uses a factory: `AddScoped(sp => new HttpClient { ... })`.

checks.label: Server section: `AddScoped<ITodoApi, ServerTodoApi>()`
checks.hint: Under `// Server: Program.cs`, write `builder.Services.AddScoped<ITodoApi, ServerTodoApi>();`.

checks.label: Client section: an `HttpClient` with `BaseAddress = new Uri(builder.HostEnvironment.BaseAddress)`
checks.hint: Under `// Client`, write `builder.Services.AddScoped(sp => new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(builder.HostEnvironment.BaseAddress) });`.

checks.label: Client section: `AddScoped<ITodoApi, HttpTodoApi>()`
checks.hint: Under `// Client: Program.cs`, write `builder.Services.AddScoped<ITodoApi, HttpTodoApi>();`.

checks.label: No Singleton for `ITodoApi`
checks.hint: Use `AddScoped` in both projects.

quiz.body: In an **Interactive Server** app, which registration gives each circuit (each user's tab) its own instance, kept across clicks and navigations?
quiz.explanation: On the server, a **scope** is a **circuit**. `AddScoped` gives one instance per circuit. Singleton is shared by all users, and Transient is new on every injection.

quiz.body: In a **WebAssembly** app, how does a service registered with `AddScoped` behave?
options: A new instance on every page navigation
A new instance on every HTTP call
Like a singleton: one instance for the app running in that tab
quiz.explanation: WebAssembly has no circuits or requests to scope by. The app has one scope for its whole life in the tab, so Scoped acts like **Singleton**. Each tab still has its own app, so nothing is shared between users.

quiz.body: A page renders with **static SSR** (no interactivity) and injects a Scoped service. How long does that instance live?
options: Until the user closes the tab
quiz.explanation: Without interactivity there is no circuit. Each **HTTP request** has its own scope, so a Scoped service is created for the request and disposed when the response is done.

quiz.body: Which line correctly injects a logger into `Index.razor`?
quiz.explanation: The syntax is **`@inject Type PropertyName`**. `ILogger<T>` is built in, so nothing needs to be registered.

quiz.body: An AI tool registered `AddSingleton<CurrentUser>()` in a Blazor Server app. `CurrentUser` stores the logged-in user's name. What is the problem?
options: Nothing: Singleton is the fastest lifetime
Singletons can't be injected into components
Every user shares the same `CurrentUser`, so users can see each other's data
The name is lost on every click
quiz.explanation: On the server, a Singleton is **one object for the whole process**, shared by every circuit. Per-user state must be **Scoped**. This is a real data leak, not just a bug.

quiz.body: Why do the docs recommend `IDbContextFactory<T>` instead of injecting `DbContext` in **Blazor Server** components?
options: A `DbContext` would live for the whole circuit, and it is not thread-safe, so overlapping queries fail
`DbContext` can't be registered in Blazor Server
The factory makes queries run in the browser
The factory caches the query results for all users
quiz.explanation: `AddDbContext` registers the context as Scoped, which on the server means **per circuit**: long-lived, tracking more and more entities, and failing when two operations overlap. A factory gives a **short-lived context per operation**, disposed with `using`.

quiz.body: A service registered with `AddTransient` implements `IDisposable`. It is injected into components in an Interactive Server app. When is each instance disposed?
options: When the scope ends, which is when the circuit ends
quiz.explanation: The container keeps transient disposables and disposes them when **their scope** ends. In Blazor Server that is the circuit, so they pile up in memory while the user stays. Use Scoped, a factory, or `OwningComponentBase`.

quiz.body: A component has `@inherits OwningComponentBase<IDraftService>`. What does it get?
options: A `Service` property from a new scope that is disposed with the component
quiz.explanation: `OwningComponentBase<T>` creates a **scope for this component**. `Service` comes from that scope, and the scope (with its Scoped and transient services) is **disposed when the component is disposed**.

quiz.body: An `InteractiveAuto` page works on the first visit, but later fails with *There is no registered service of type 'ITodoApi'*. What is the most likely cause?
options: `ITodoApi` is registered only in the **server** `Program.cs`, not in the `.Client` one
quiz.explanation: Later visits run in **WebAssembly**, which uses the **client** container. Register an implementation (often an `HttpClient`-based one) in the `.Client` `Program.cs` too.

quiz.body: Which service is **not** available by default in a server-side Blazor app, so you must register it before you inject it?
quiz.explanation: `NavigationManager`, `IJSRuntime` and `ILogger<T>` are built in. `HttpClient` is registered by the WebAssembly template in the `.Client` project, but on the server you add it yourself, usually with `builder.Services.AddHttpClient()`.

interview.question: What is dependency injection, and how do you use it in Blazor?
interview.modelAnswer: A class asks for its dependencies instead of creating them, and a container provides them. In Blazor you register services in `Program.cs` (for example `AddScoped<IService, Impl>()`), then inject them with `@inject` in markup or `[Inject]` in code-behind.

interview.question: What are the three service lifetimes?
interview.modelAnswer: Singleton: one instance for the whole app. Scoped: one instance per scope. Transient: a new instance every time it is injected.

interview.question: What does Scoped mean in Blazor?
interview.modelAnswer: It depends on where the code runs. In static SSR, a scope is one HTTP request. In Interactive Server, it is one circuit, so one user's tab. In WebAssembly, it is the app in the tab, so Scoped acts like a singleton.

interview.question: Why is a Singleton with user data dangerous in Blazor Server?
interview.modelAnswer: On the server one Singleton instance is shared by every user and circuit, so one user can see another user's data. It must also be thread-safe. Per-user state should be Scoped.

interview.question: How do you use Entity Framework Core in a Blazor Server component?
interview.modelAnswer: Register `AddDbContextFactory`, inject `IDbContextFactory<T>`, and create a short-lived context per operation with `using var db = await factory.CreateDbContextAsync()`. Injecting `DbContext` directly makes it live for the whole circuit, and it is not thread-safe.

interview.question: What is `OwningComponentBase` for?
interview.modelAnswer: It gives a component its own DI scope, so Scoped and transient services live only as long as the component. `OwningComponentBase<T>` exposes the service as `Service`; the base version exposes `ScopedServices`. The scope is disposed with the component.

interview.question: What must you do with services for components that use Auto or WebAssembly render modes?
interview.modelAnswer: Register them in the `.Client` `Program.cs` too, because in the browser the component uses the client container. Often the interface lives in the client project, with a server implementation that reads the database and a client implementation that calls an API.

interview.question: What is the problem with transient services that implement `IDisposable` in Blazor Server?
interview.modelAnswer: The container keeps them and disposes them only when the scope ends, which is when the circuit ends. So they stay in memory while the user is connected. Use Scoped, a factory, or `OwningComponentBase` instead.
